Family notes & prerequisites for known issues
  • After a reload the Task List (and tab bar entry) appears only once history has loaded; wait about 2 s before counting [data-active="true"] rows.
  • [data-active] is also used by sidebar conversation cards: always combine it with has-text=<task title>.
  • browser click --observe takes a plain CSS selector ('[data-testid=compact-context-button]'); the testid= form fails with a querySelectorAll SyntaxError.
  • "Create a plan" leaves that conversation in plan mode: the next composer message goes to the planner helper, which has no launch_child_conversation or canvas_ui_control. Use a separate conversation for client-tool prompts.
  • The child-launch toast's Open link animates; browser click on it times out with "element is not stable". Read the child id from the parent's [child-conversation] message instead.
  • GET …/file/download?path=…/.agents_tmp/PLAN.md 404 and GET /api/llm/balance 404 are expected app-origin errors (no plan yet; no balance endpoint). Count them in browser errors --app-only but do not report them.
  • Escape closes the composer context popover and the Overview "..." menu and returns focus to the trigger (#18044); an outside click, or a second click on the trigger, closes them too.
  • The Overview column is 28 px narrower than its content (scrollWidth 296, clientWidth 268). After some clicks inside it, Playwright's scroll-into-view shifts it and the card looks cut off on the left; browser reload restores it before taking screenshots.
  • The agent may summarize a client-tool action with its own title (for example "Launch local child conversation to reply PONG") instead of "Launching a child conversation"; assert the toast and events, not the chat title.
  • The Overview peek appears only while the drawer is open (canPeekOnHover needs isRightPanelShown); a browser goto or reload starts with the drawer closed.
  • The Overview's repo and branch rows depend on a bash probe (useLocalGitInfo) that runs only while the conversation's status is idle, running, waiting for confirmation or finished and the agent is not in error. Right after conversation start the probe has run and its result stays cached on the page, but on an errored conversation a reload hides the rows again, and conversation pause does not apply to an errored conversation. Read the rows before any goto or reload.
  • At phone width (and in a narrow drawer) the tab row shows only the tabs that fit; the rest are reachable only through the tabs menu (conversation-tabs-menu-open-<tab>), and which tabs fit depends on the active tab's label width.
  • Plain agent-canvas instances on one machine share the tmux socket /tmp/tmux-<uid>/openhands (OpenHands/OpenHands#17946), so another instance stopping can reset this one's terminal. control-openhands launch gives each run its own TMUX_TMPDIR, so in verification runs a reset means this run's agent server restarted.
  • Agent Tools & Metadata remembers the last tab (it reopens on Available Tools).
  • The Overview menu opens only Pull Requests (conversation-overview-menu-open-git-pull_requests); its testids are conversation-overview-menu-open-* and -pin-* for workspace and the Git rows only.
  • Known open issues: terminal history after reload (#17566) still fails (reproduced 2026-10-06); info modals at phone width (#17562) pass.
  • Agent tab requests (open_tab, navigate_to_file, chat file links) are saved per conversation like a user tab click (#18045): after the agent opens Terminal or a file and the page reloads, the drawer starts closed and the panel toggle reopens it on that tab; clicking that tab then closes the drawer. At phone width they navigate to /conversations/<id>/panel.
  • Known issue #17774 (F27.planner-empty F27.planner-plan): Planner reads on a native Windows local backend reject drive-letter/mixed-separator workspace paths with Conversation file path must stay inside the workspace before a download request. Recheck both a scratch workspace and an opened drive-letter workspace, with and without .agents_tmp/PLAN.md; this run lacks a Windows local Agent Server.
  • Known issue #17198 (F27.terminal-output): Native Windows desktop agents intermittently return [Command finished execution with no output] for real file-listing/terminal commands and retry them. Recheck with the affected Windows installer/runtime, project agent definitions and an exact command/workspace; no deterministic pattern or backend trace is provided, and this run has no Windows desktop runtime. The backend counterpart is OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#4963.
  • Known issue #16551 (F27.browser-screenshot): On native Windows, the browser tool chooses system Chrome over installed Playwright Chromium and times out before returning state/screenshots. Recheck default browser selection and an explicit executable-path control on a Windows host with both browsers and the reported browser_use runtime; the verification Chromium itself is a different tool. Blocked here without Windows and real browser-tool execution credentials.
  • Known issue #16581 (F27.terminal-output): A module-scoped terminal command index can suppress output in a second simultaneously mounted Terminal and reset the first when either unmounts. The report describes a future split-panel/embedded concurrent mount rather than a supported standalone entry point. Recheck in a host that actually mounts two independent Canvas Terminal consumers with real command histories; the current harness has one Terminal route and no such host fixture.
  • Known issue #17384 (F27.launch-child): A file-based delegated subagent using a saved profile/provider connection can fail with HTTP 401 while the top-level conversation succeeds, because encrypted provider credentials are not decrypted in that backend factory path. Recheck a reviewed .agents/agents/ worker, encrypted provider connection and saved profile using a real key, comparing parent and worker authentication. This is a delegated SDK subagent path, distinct from the client-tool child-launch recipe; neither a dummy key nor an unencrypted profile proves it.
  • Known issue OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5533 (F27.terminal-output): A slow interactive Bash startup can make the first terminal command return early with empty output and a false successful exit code. Recheck both standalone and pooled tmux using a private .bashrc with sleep 0.4, then a bounded sleep 2 first command and its real observation. The shell fixture can be arranged, but the mapped agent-command/Terminal path cannot run here without a model key.
  • Known issue OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5322 (F27.terminal-output): The default tmux pane pool or Windows terminal can let git log -p start an interactive pager, so the next agent command receives stale paged output instead of its own result. Recheck a reviewed large git fixture, a real installed pager and a follow-up marker command on each affected terminal backend. The fixture is arrangeable, but the mapped agent-tool path needs a model key (and the Windows half needs Windows).
  • Known issue #17383 (F27.browser-screenshot; dependency counterpart OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5152): unlocked dependency resolution can silently remove the agent's browser tools. The actual 2026-10-12 pinned runtime resolves browser-use 0.11.13, mcp 1.30.0 and fastmcp 3.4.8; its genuine BrowserToolExecutor constructs successfully. That narrowly fails to reproduce the SDK report's specified mcp 2.x import failure. Fresh constructor recheck on 2026-10-16 at b34ac59, using the actual Agent Server 1.55.0 interpreter and private HOME, again resolves browser-use 0.11.13, mcp 1.30.0 and fastmcp 3.4.8 and constructs successfully; no browser operation or model was run. The Canvas/global browser-operation path still needs an authorized real LLM and a genuine browser-enabled agent issuing a browser_* operation; construction alone does not establish that feature works.
  • Browser availability also depends on OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5899 (F27.browser-screenshot; canonical tool-selection note in F13): a Chromium installed only under PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH is missed by the agent-tool probe. Recheck the real browser-tool operation on a host with only that custom cache and no standard browser, default cache or PATH executable. This Mac's user Chrome must remain installed; an executor constructor or the verification browser is not a successful agent browser operation.
  • Known issue OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5835 (F27.overview-identity): the local Overview Git probe uses conversation-scoped Bash execution; an idle-eviction pass can kill scoped work without a final output. Recheck a disposable short-idle-TTL server while a genuine Canvas Git probe is still executing, with independently observed command lifetime and the eventual output/result. The report's standalone asynchronous sleep reproduction is supporting backend evidence, not proof of a Terminal-tab command, which uses the agent event stream instead.

Family notes & prerequisites for known issues
  • A toast can cover the toolbar (Save draft, Test, Close) and stays while the pointer rests on it, so the next toolbar click times out ("subtree intercepts pointer events"). After each save, browser hover a form field (for example testid=automation-setup-name) before clicking the toolbar again, as F22's Gotchas say.
  • Drive inputs with browser fill: setting .value from browser eval does not reach React state for every field, and a save then sends the old value.
  • Change one field per Save draft when checking a validation message: a save shows only the first server error, so two edits in one save hide the second.
  • A cold load of /automations/setup?draftId=<id> or ?automationId=<id> (a reload or a typed URL) opens the form: re-checked 2026-10-14 on a control-openhands launch of main with this family (both read their Name back). An earlier instance of unknown build stayed on Loading saved draft… for more than 20 s; if that returns, compare with opening the same draft from the dashboard.
  • The draft bar duplicates the prompt error: Field required appears both under Prompt and in the bar.
  • Kebab Edit on a Custom Python automation shows the code editor instead of the saved bundle summary: open bug #18341 (F23), with fixes in PRs #18353 and #18444.
  • Escape on the setup page does nothing, by design (F23.edit-close).

Before you start

Use an OpenHands checkout at the source revision, with Node 24+, installed npm dependencies, uv / uvx, and a supported Chromium browser. The verification skill is the complete setup contract.

export PATH="$PWD/.agents/skills/verify-openhands/scripts:$PATH"
export OH_VERIFY_RUN=$(control-openhands launch --new --print-run)
control-openhands doctor
control-openhands onboard --skip
# Configure a model only for a scenario that needs one:
control-openhands llm preset deepseek
# When the run is complete:
control-openhands stop

F01 walks onboarding instead of skipping it. No-model checks run before model configuration. Keep OH_VERIFY_RUN set so commands address your own run. Desktop is 1440 × 1000; phone is 390 × 844. Model-backed checks need the configured provider key and budget.

Recipes run in source order within each family and can share fixtures. The page preserves that order; “as above” is a dependency on an earlier case. Setup commands and API writes arrange state. They do not prove a UI path. Follow the family cleanup steps.

A known failure preserves the intended expectation beside the observed defect. Executable known-bug blocks use xfail for a reproduced symptom and xpass when it stops reproducing. Cloud accounts, enterprise capabilities and other unavailable prerequisites remain explicit. “Not run” is different from “blocked”.

The maintained map describes application behavior at its pinned revision. Once a fix is verified in the application version under test, remove the obsolete failure note and keep the normal expectation. Dated evidence belongs in the backfill ledger.

Read the full map index and coverage boundaries, the CLI guide, or the earlier illustrated edition. The verification approach adapts Lauren Tan’s (@poteto) pstack verification-skill generators; attribution and adaptation.
